title: WTI: delivery and scarce storage

sources.sourceRole: Primary publication; account may be retrospective or interested-party

documentedClaim: The EIA links negative near-expiry prices to low liquidity and scarce available storage.
inferredMechanism: Physical delivery obligations and capacity constraints can dominate usual price relationships.
counterevidence: A price that looks cheap may be expensive for a holder unable to take delivery.
transferRequirements: Do not assume storage, transport or delivery access. Preserve contract-specific expiry and roll semantics; retain as an access-dependent lead.
outcomeBoundary: Public narrative already inspected; described cases are discovery examples, never untouched confirmation. No experimental market outcome dataset opened.
